title: Add `BitField[T]` type to GDScript
body:
This PR introduces an analyzer-only type called `BitField`, used to determine if an enum should be treated as a bitfield, to GDScript.

- Gives `PROPERTY_HINT_FLAGS` and `PROPERTY_USAGE_CLASS_IS_BITFIELD` to variables of this type.
- Ignores `ENUM_VARIABLE_WITHOUT_DEFAULT`, `INT_AS_ENUM_WITHOUT_CAST` and `INT_AS_ENUM_WITHOUT_MATCH`.
- **Must** have one collection type (which has to be an enum), unlike other collection types that are currently supported.
- At runtime and compile-time, it is treated as a regular integer.

Usage:
```gdscript
enum MyEnum {
    FIRST = 1 << 0,
    SECOND = 1 << 1,
    THIRD = 1 << 2,
    FOURTH = 1 << 3    
}

@export var bitfield: BitField[MyEnum]
# This has the same effect, but has weaker static typing and can be annoying to setup for larger enums
@export_flags("First", "Second", "Third", "Fourth") var flags: int

# Obviously, it's not restricted to just being used in @export, 
# although I don't see much of a point, other than for documentation purposes.
func my_func(param: BitField[MyEnum]) -> BitField[MyEnum]:
    return MyEnum.FIRST | MyEnum.SECOND

signal my_signal(param: BitField[MyEnum])
```

This is also _technically_ the first collection type to support being nested, but since it's just treated as an int at compile-time, it doesn't really count in my book:
```gdscript
var array: Array[BitField[EnumName]]
var dict: Dictionary[BitField[EnumName], BitField[EnumName]]
```

Unfortunately, due to this not being a real type, it cannot have methods to make usage easier. What would be an ideal implementation is making [the existing BitField type in the core](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/core/templates/bit_field.h) available in GDScript, but this would require a much more complicated implementation, which is probably not worth it.

Known issues:
- Trying to ctrl+click on a `BitField` type in the script editor does not lead to it's documentation page, unlike other types. I can't seem to figure out where the logic for this is.

Supersedes #117381.
Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/923.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
+<class name="BitField" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="../class.xsd">
+	<brief_description>
+		A GDScript-only type that represents an integer composed as a bitmask of other flags.
+	</brief_description>
+	<description>
+		A type to define enums as bitfield. Certain warnings that would normally be raised when exporting or returning enums will automatically get ignored. When exporting this type, it will automatically obtain [constant PROPERTY_HINT_FLAGS] and [constant PROPERTY_USAGE_CLASS_IS_BITFIELD], similar to [annotation @GDScript.@export_flags].
+		When passed around, this type behaves like a regular integer. This type supports being nested into other collection types.
+		[b]Note:[/b] This type cannot be inferred, it has to be specified.
+		[b]Note:[/b] Languages other than GDScript may define bitfields in their own way. For example, in C#, enums are marked with the [code][Flags][/code] attribute, which has the same effect.
+		Example:
+		[codeblock]
+		enum Direction {
+			LEFT = 1,
+			RIGHT = 2,
+			UP = 4,
+			DOWN = 8,
+		}
+
+		# Usage:
+		@export var direction: BitField[Direction]
+		@export var regular_enum: Direction # Raises ENUM_VARIABLE_WITHOUT_DEFAULT.
+
+		# Nesting is supported:
+		@export var array: Array[BitField[Direction]]
+		@export var dict: Dictionary[BitField[Direction], BitField[Direction]]
+
+		func return_regular_enum() -> Direction:
+			return Direction.LEFT | Direction.RIGHT # Raises INT_AS_ENUM_WITHOUT_CAST and INT_AS_ENUM_WITHOUT_MATCH.
+
+		func return_bitfield() -> BitField[Direction]:
+			return Direction.LEFT | Direction.RIGHT # No warnings.
+		[/codeblock]
+	</description>
+	<tutorials>
+	</tutorials>
+</class>
